name: p2-opentitan-uart-serial-peer-f1f5
description: One Ibex RVFI OBI CPU and the pinned OpenTitan UART TL-UL target with the host itself as the serial peer: the host clocks a complete 8n1 frame onto the device's rx pin at the declared bit period and decodes the byte the device serializes on its tx pin, with the sticky tx_done interrupt taken and cleared as F5.
notes: the serial peer is declared in configs/behaviors/opentitan_uart_serial_peer_f5.json: rx_role 'rx', tx_role 'tx', tx_en_role 'tx_en', idle_level 1, bit_ticks 32 and frame 8n1. The bit period is not a measurement: uart_core.sv's NCO carry fires every second cycle at ctrl.nco=0x8000 and one bit is sixteen of those ticks, so 32 host cycles per bit

rx=1 is the line's idle level, applied by the generated binding as the declared fixed input and then owned by the host driver: the peer rests the pin at idle_level and drives the frame's bits for exactly bit_ticks each

the RX half of the run is the FIFO_STATUS read with a stimulus byte: the host drives a complete frame with the CPU clock parked, so the device already holds the byte when the CPU reads its status word (RXLVL is bits 23:16 of FIFO_STATUS at 0x24) and then its data register (RDATA at 0x18). The TX half is the F5 case: the firmware writes WDATA at 0x1c, the device serializes it, the host decodes the byte from the tx pin and the device's own tx_done output is delivered, taken and W1C-cleared
the UART profile's own MMIO endpoint is tl-ul/1 with integrity required, so the target is a TL-UL target behind the real beat_to_tlul adapter; no APB3 target is in this build
no DMA is declared, so F6 is refused by name as unsupported-f6:no-dma-model:TL-UL
this file declares the scenario; it is not evidence. The run under runs/p2-pins-serial-20261103/ is the evidence
